page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 4 vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and 2 threads per core running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory. The hardware configuration includes a dedicated NVIDIA T4 GPU from the Turing architecture with 16 GB of VRAM, alongside 125 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance split. Standard CPU and memory operations, such as stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests, fall into the lower performance tiers, reflecting the modest capabilities of its 4 vCPUs. However, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers strong results for machine learning tasks. LLM inference speeds for prompt processing with small (135M) and medium (7B) models rank in the top tier, while text generation speeds for these models are rated as strong.

From a resource density perspective, the g4dn.xlarge offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads without requiring massive CPU or memory allocations. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage and dedicated GPU memory makes it highly suitable for small to medium machine learning inference, graphics-intensive applications, and lightweight CUDA-based development, whereas general-purpose compute-heavy tasks are constrained by the lower-tier CPU performance.
